results.title: A Tale of Two Capitals — The End of Everywhere
results.content:
La Paz is the administrative capital of Bolivia and is where the seat of government is today. Sucre is the constitutional capital of the country, the first capital and - according to the latest constitution of the country, the only actual real capital. It’s a sore point for some - less than 150 years ago the people of Sucre fought a civil war with La Paz to assert their title as capital city. [...] #### La Paz

As mentioned, La Paz is the administrative capital of Bolivia, known for its dramatic geography where it sits in a deep valley surrounded by the high Andes Mountains.

It is one of the highest “capital cities” in the world, with its altitude reaching over 4,000 meters in the highest neighborhoods.

results.title: Bolivia Has Two Capitals: Sucre & La Paz Explained
results.content:
Sucre is the constitutional capital of Bolivia. La Paz is the seat of government and the place most travelers think of as the capital. Understanding why Bolivia works this way adds depth to any visit, helps explain the country’s political and cultural identity, and makes travel here more meaningful. [...] ## What Is the Capital of Bolivia?

The official capital of Bolivia is Sucre. This is written into the Bolivian Constitution.  
   
 At the same time, La Paz functions as the administrative capital of Bolivia. It’s where the president, the legislature, and most government offices are located. This is why La Paz is often called the capital city of Bolivia in everyday use, even though it is not the constitutional capital.

## Frequently Asked Questions About the Capital of Bolivia

Which Is the True Capital of Bolivia?

Sucre is the true and official capital of Bolivia, as stated in the constitution. La Paz is the seat of government.

Why Does Bolivia Have Two Capitals?

The split dates back to the Federal War of 1899. It was a political compromise between regions, allowing both cities to keep national importance.

La Paz is the state capital and center of commerce, as well as the home of the three leading marine biology institutes in Latin America (UABCS, CIBNOR & CICIMAR), largely because it sits on the Gulf of California, which is home to exceptional marine biodiversity. It also supports several other university-level institutes of learning, such as the Universidad Autonoma de Baja California Sur. [...] La Paz (pronounced ( "Help:IPA/Spanish") ⓘ, English: "peace") is the capital and largest city of the Mexican state of Baja California Sur, with a population of 250,141 in the 2020 census. La Paz is located in La Paz Municipality, the fourth-largest municipality in Mexico by area (20,275 km2 (7,828 sq mi)), with a population of 292,241. The city proper of La Paz is the main population center in Baja California Sur and accounts for almost one-third of the population of the state.
